idiom_name: hand-written wrapper type per interface (embed the interface, override every mediated method)
implementation_notes: Go has no dynamic proxies: an interface value's method set is fixed at compile time, and a wrapper must be a defined type that implements the same interface method by method. The idiomatic shape embeds the wrapped interface (which promotes every method) and overrides the methods the membrane mediates; the promoted methods keep working unmediated, so any member that accepts or returns an interface value must be overridden to wrap it - that is the manual part. Identity is pointer comparison on the concrete target, so the registry is a map keyed by that pointer (never by interface value, which panics for uncomparable dynamic types), and revocation is a mutex-guarded flag or generation counter read and used in one critical section. Because there is no interception hook, completeness is enforced by review and tests rather than by the runtime - which is exactly why embedding the interface is a hazard and explicit forwarding is safer when the surface is security-relevant.
pitfalls: Embedding the interface promotes every method, including ones that hand out raw values: a method added to the interface silently adds an unmediated route through the membrane unless the wrapper overrides it.

Interface identity is not pointer identity: two interface values holding the same object compare unequal when their dynamic types differ, and comparing interfaces whose dynamic type is uncomparable panics at run time - key the identity map on the concrete pointer instead.

A long-lived registry that holds the targets strongly retains the whole graph; revocation must clear it, not just set a flag, and every method must still be guarded so a stale wrapper cannot be used after revocation.
